question: Which link carries these bits, at what latency and what cost per bit?
title: Communications Systems: A Practical Reference
lede: Every link is the same three trade-offs in a different order: how far it reaches, how much it carries, and how much of the cost is fixed before the first bit moves. This guide catalogs {{N_ENTRIES}} links, systems and practices across seven classes, with the reach and capacity each one delivers, the latency it cannot get below, and where the money actually goes — which in most networks is civil works and spectrum rather than radios.

facets.label: Reach
facets.tip: How far one hop of this link goes. Meters covers in-building and short-range · Kilometers covers a cell, a campus, or a metro span · Continental covers long-haul terrestrial and regional satellite beams · Global covers intercontinental cable and constellations. Reach and cost per bit move in opposite directions for almost every technology here.

facets.label: Capacity
facets.tip: Throughput of one link or one system, per user where that is the meaningful number and per fiber pair or per satellite where it is not. Kilobits covers telemetry and messaging · Megabits covers ordinary consumer and enterprise service · Gigabits covers modern access and backhaul · Terabits covers submarine cable and long-haul optical transport.

facets.label: Medium
facets.tip: What carries the signal, which decides what can interfere with it and who has to license it. Radio needs spectrum rights and shares its band with everyone else in it · Fiber needs a right of way and a trench · Laser needs line of sight and clear air · Acoustic is the only thing that works underwater and pays for it in bandwidth. Entries about networking practice carry no medium, because they apply to all of them.

facets.label: Latency
facets.tip: One-way delay a user sees in normal operation, including the processing the link cannot skip. This is the number that separates otherwise similar options: a geostationary satellite and a low-orbit constellation both cover a continent, and only one of them can carry a video call.

facets.label: Maturity
facets.tip: Deployed = carrying commercial traffic at scale, with a supply chain and trained installers · Scaling = commercial and growing fast, with the standard settled · Early = first commercial systems, standards still moving · Research = demonstrated, no commercial service.
